## add the visual layer to video translation


Translation and voice workflows create localized audio. Sync adapts visible speech in the source video to match that audio.


### keep your audio stack


Bring your source video and finished translated or dubbed audio into sync. once language and voice work is complete.


### add visual localization


lipsync-2 adapts visible speech to the localized audio, so the audience sees speech that matches the language they hear.


### scale repeatable delivery


Zero-shot generation lets new speakers and language versions move through the same workflow without per-speaker setup.


## route each localization project to the right model


### localize standard language versions


lipsync-2 balances realism and turnaround for repeatable video translation across everyday footage and multiple language versions.


### elevate premium localized content


lipsync-2-pro adds facial detail for close-ups and high-visibility scenes where translated versions need a more polished finish.


### handle complex localized shots


sync-3 uses scene context to help handle difficult shots with varied poses, lighting, framing, and obstructions.

## how sync. fits into video translation


Localized audio enters sync. after language and voice work. The resulting picture goes into your existing quality control (QC) and delivery workflow.


### where sync. integrates


Provide the source video and completed localized audio after translation and voice work. Review visually synced picture before final delivery.


### QC rounds


1.


**Sample calibration.** Validate visual and creative alignment on a short sample.


2.


**Full-version review.** Inspect the synced picture, exceptions, and difficult shots.


3.


**Revision and delivery.** Apply consolidated notes and return approved outputs.


## built for repeatable localization operations


-


**Batch generation.** Queue up to 500 short lip sync jobs per request on approved plans. See the[Batch API guide](https://sync.so/docs/api-reference/guides/batch-processing) for clip limits and access.


-


**API and Python/TypeScript SDKs.** Add visual sync to your localization systems.


-


**Async jobs and webhooks.** Automate status updates, handoffs, and downstream actions.


-


**Cost estimation.** Estimate generation costs before production begins.


-


**Zero-shot models.** Support new speakers without character-specific training.


-


**Professional outputs.** Managed workflows can support ProRes and high-resolution delivery.


-


**Flexible storage.** Discuss client-side storage or managed private S3 for managed workflows.


## choose how you edit


Start with the workflow that matches the shot, then move into the timeline when you need more control.


### bring finished dialogue


In Studio’s lip sync workflow, upload the shot, add the localized audio, pick a model, and generate the new take.


### translate and dub in Studio


Choose a supported target language in Translate & Dub to generate dubbed audio and visual sync in the same workflow.


### edit on the timeline


Use the timeline editor to trim, split, and position audio for precise dialogue timing.[Explore Studio workflows.](https://sync.so/docs/web-app-guides/studio-workflows)
